# Iteration 2 {.unnumbered}

In Iteration 1, you moved quickly through the complete machine-learning workflow and built your first classification, regression and clustering models.

In Iteration 2, you will go through the workflow again, but this time **in greater depth**. The work is still structured: notebooks and resources will guide you through the main steps.

## Task 2 — Business Understanding

Before going deeper into the data, develop enough domain understanding to reason about what you are modelling.

Read:

- [SMILES: A Simplified Chemical Language](PATH-TO-PDF)

Your goal is **not to master chemistry**. Focus on understanding what SMILES strings represent and how they describe molecular structure.

## Task 3 — Data Understanding

Explore the HOPV data, identify inputs and targets, investigate data quality, and examine important distributions and relationships.

Complete **in order**:

1. [Understanding HOPV Stability](i2_t3_nb1_understanding_hopv_stability_csv.ipynb)
2. [Understanding HOMO/LUMO Data](i2_t3_nb2_understanding_hopv_homolumo_data.ipynb)

## Task 4 — Data Preparation

Turn the raw molecular data into data suitable for machine-learning models.

Complete:

- [Data Preparation](i2_t4_nb1_data_prep.ipynb)

## Task 5 — Classification

Build a classification model to predict molecular stability.

Complete:

- [Classification](i2_t5_nb1_classification.ipynb)

## Task 6 — Regression

Build regression models to predict HOMO and LUMO energy levels.

Complete:

- [Regression](i2_t6_nb1_regression.ipynb)

## Task 7 — Clustering

Use clustering to investigate molecular structure and identify patterns that may also be useful for your supervised models.

Complete:

- [Clustering](i2_t7_nb1_clustering.ipynb)

## Keep iterating

Although the notebooks above provide a structured path, the workflow is not strictly linear.

What you discover during modelling may give you a reason to return to your data, change its preparation, investigate a new feature, or revisit your understanding of the problem.

Iteration 3+ will make this process increasingly open-ended.
